title: Hardware Configuration Baseline: the released foxBMS 2 board set

standards_mappings.reference: Part 5, Clause 7 (configuration management of hardware items)
standards_mappings.rationale: A configuration baseline is the precondition a hardware requirements analysis and a hardware integration and test plan are both written against; this record supplies the item set and the exact released versions.
Names the configuration the existing hardware technical requirements apply to. It does not analyse anything and does not supply the HW Interface Requirements family HWE.1 expects.
Identifies which released boards constitute the hardware set, which is the input a hardware architecture would allocate over. No architecture, block diagram or interface schematic record is supplied.
Fixes the configuration a hardware integration and test plan is scoped against, so that the plan has a defined subject. The plan itself is FB2-HW-HVP-000001 and it has no executed step.

revision_history.author: hw_engineer
revision_history.description: First record in this corpus to identify the hardware configuration at all. Every board id, item label, version, release archive name and release URL is transcribed from hardware/README.md, the only file under hardware/, and every derived count is mechanically reproducible from that file. Recorded as origin=derived because the content is derived from a tracked first-party file rather than synthesised.

baseline_subject.description: The set of foxBMS 2 printed circuit boards that the project publishes as released hardware, with the exact version of each release, and the status of each board's design artefacts as seen from this repository.
baseline_subject.authority: hardware/README.md - the hardware release index of the foxBMS 2 project
baseline_subject.derivation: Every row of the release index that begins with a pipe and carries a Version cell was parsed: the Item string, the Version string and the href of the File cell were taken verbatim. The release URL is that href; the release archive name is its last path segment. No row was added, merged, deduplicated or reordered. Counts are: 10 release rows across 7 distinct Item strings.

components.name: SUFFIX
components.meaning: A number appended after a hyphen for changes made in the Altium projects that are not related to the schematic or the layout, where it would be wrong to bump MAJOR, MINOR or PATCH because the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version string is printed on the hardware.

versioning_scheme.suffix_rationale: The authority file gives the reason for the suffix explicitly: a change confined to the Altium project metadata does not change the hardware that was built, and the version string is printed on the hardware, so the numeric part is held and a suffix is incremented instead.
versioning_scheme.authority_quote_basis: Derived from the 'Hardware Versioning' section of hardware/README.md, which states that the basic pattern is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with MAJOR, MINOR and PATCH as numbers, that the full version identifier of a hardware release is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-SUFFIX where SUFFIX is a number, and that the README always points to a generic link of the latest released version, i.e. the one with the latest suffix.
observations: No version printed in the release index carries a suffix: all ten are plain MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

The suffix does appear in two changelog headings, so the scheme is in use: the master changelog heads the released master version 'v1.2.3-0' and the MC33775A changelog heads the released version 'v1.0.3-0'. Both released versions are printed without the suffix in the release index. This record records both spellings and corrects neither.

The authority file states that it always points to a generic link of the latest released version, but the release index lists more than one version per board for three boards, each with a version-specific archive name, so the release index is a list of releases rather than a single latest link per board.

inventory_counts.derivation: Release rows are the table rows of hardware/README.md that carry a Version cell: TI BMS-Master 1.2.3; LTC Interface (LTC6820) 1.0.3; NXP Interface (MC33664) 1.0.2; MAXIM Interface (MAX17841b) 1.0.0; LTC 12 Cell Slave (LTC6811-1) 2.1.5 and 2.1.7; LTC 18 Cell Slave (LTC6813-1) 1.1.3, 1.1.5 and 1.1.6; NXP 14 Cell Slave (MC33775A) 1.0.3. Distinct board designations are the distinct Item strings among those rows, which is 7.
count_disagreements_recorded: The figure 8 is sometimes given for the size of this board set. It is reproducible from hardware/README.md under no rule applied to that file: the file yields 7 distinct board designations and 10 release rows, and 8 matches neither. This record states the two figures the file does support and does not carry the 8 forward, because carrying a number that the authority file does not yield would be exactly the kind of untraceable count this corpus exists to remove.

Counting released boards as 10 (one per release row) and counting board designs as 7 (one per Item string) are both defensible; which one a reader wants depends on whether they are counting what can be built (a version) or what exists (a design). Both are recorded so neither reader has to guess.

documentation_inventory.statement: A separate and substantial hardware documentation tree is tracked in this repository at docs/hardware/. At commit 308028fb it holds 166 tracked files, of which 93 are CSV tables (pinouts, electrical ratings, connector pin assignments, mechanical dimensions) and 26 are draw.io diagram sources, plus per-version release notes in reStructuredText and one changelog per board family. It holds no Altium source file. The distinction matters and is recorded because it is easy to get wrong in either direction: hardware/README.md is not the only first-party hardware evidence in this repository, and docs/hardware/ is not a substitute for the design sources, which remain external. Where this repository can verify a hardware claim at all, it is against these tables and notes.

design_artefact_availability.search_performed: git ls-tree -r --name-only 308028fb -- hardware/ returns exactly one path, hardware/README.md, which is the whole of the hardware/ tree. git log --all --name-only --diff-filter=A -- '*.SchDoc' '*.PcbDoc' '*.PrjPcb' returns no output, so no Altium source file was ever added to any branch of this repository. git ls-tree -r --name-only 308028fb -- docs/hardware/ returns 166 documentation files and no Altium source file.
design_artefact_availability.search_result: Zero Altium design source files, in the working tree and in every commit of every branch. The design sources for all seven boards live outside this repository.
design_artefact_availability.access_conditions: The designs are published as per-release zip archives on an external Fraunhofer IISB server. This corpus does not hold credentials for that server, does not claim to, and did not attempt a download. The archives are proprietary CAD and are not readable by an offline text corpus in any case, so obtaining them would not make a schematic, layout or BOM verifiable here.
design_artefact_availability.consequence: No board-level design content may be authored from this repository: not a net, not a reference designator, not a component, not a register, not an offset. Where a claim about the hardware would require one of those, this corpus has no basis for it and says so rather than supplying one. See FB2-HW-HDD-000001 for the recorded consequence for HWE.3.

variant_cross_reference.statement: The variant registry names nine board designations; six of them are boards this record's release index releases and three are not. Two of the three are documented in this repository but released nowhere: the ADI ADES1830 has per-version release notes and a full artefact set for v0.9.0 under docs/hardware/slaves/16-adi-ades1830-vx.x.x/, and the LTC6804-1 has a note whose version component is the literal x.x.x. The third, HW-BMS-SLAVE-14-MAX17852, has exactly one tracked file under its tree, docs/hardware/slaves/14-maxim-max17852-vx.x.x/.dummy. The disagreement runs in both directions: the release index sells the 12-cell LTC6811-1 slave at two versions and the registry names no board designation for it, because that designation exists in docs/artifacts/sources/source-inventory.json rather than in the registry. This record states the reconciliation and edits neither file. The single place where two first-party files genuinely conflict is the ADES1830, whose variant note asserts that a hardware design package is available while the release index contains no ADI board at any version; 'available' and 'released' are different claims and the release index supports only the second. The full reconciliation, including the one variant that names no board at all, is FB2-SYS-HVA-000001.

not_established_by_this_record: No schematic, PCB layout, bill of materials or component specification. None can be authored from this repository because the Altium sources are external and were never present in any commit.
No net, reference designator, component, register, memory-mapped offset, mask or base address. Those live in the external design sources and in the device data sheets this corpus does not hold.
No verification result of any kind. This record identifies a configuration; it does not test, inspect or demonstrate that any board conforms to anything.

No confirmation that a released version is manufacturable, that its documentation matches its design, or that the archives on the external server still resolve. The URLs are transcribed from the index, not fetched.

No statement about which board version any particular vehicle, test bench or hardware-in-the-loop rig is fitted with. That is fleet and test-rig configuration data, and this repository does not hold it.
No ASIL, no conformity claim, no certification, no supplier qualification, no human approval and no ASPICE capability level.

authority_and_independence.independence_statement: This record was authored by an AI agent reading hardware/README.md and the docs/hardware/ tree. It is therefore a transcription and a mechanical derivation, not an independent configuration audit. No hardware engineer has reviewed it, no board has been inspected, and no claim in it has been checked against a physical board or against a design source. An AI-authored artefact is not independent evidence.
